newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares flat, seen capped by primary offers.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares flat, seen capped by primary offers.

text.p: Polish shares stabilised in higher volume and were expected to stay in their 2.5-month sideways drift in the next few weeks as the primary market was seen drawing investor interest and capital from the bourse.

The main market's WIG index inched up 1.6 points to 16,002.2 points, and turnover rose 6.7 percent to 126.8 million zlotys ($39.6 million) on all three markets as 63 issues rose, 27 fell and 15 were flat.
"The current situation (on the bourse) is caused by primary offers and in the near-term one shouldn't expect it to change," said Tomasz Cwintal, an analyst at BGZ brokerage.
Analysts said any deeper falls were also unlikely because the current prices, with the average 1996 P/E ratio of 15.8 did not justify falls below 15,500.

Analysts said one-billion-zloty Bank Handlowy SA public offering, now underway, and KGHM Polska Miedz offering starting on June 30 and worth at least 300 million zlotys ($93 million) in the domestic tranche, were cooling demand for listed stocks.
Some analysts said the bourse was more likely to test its downside because the general elections due in September would additionally limit buying.
